text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Lim Wee Kiak –  17  To ask	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the Ministry doing to address teen suicides; (b) whether the Ministry has done any studies on reducing the suicide rate; and (c) what is the Ministry doing to strengthen the current multi-Ministry approach on this issue.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry will consider launching a suicide prevention campaign to raise awareness on how to look out for tell-tale signs to prevent suicides; (b) whether there is a need to set up a special hotline for teens which is manned by teenagers trained in counselling; and (c) whether counsellors are trained to alert the parents/guardians if they counsel a potentially suicidal teen.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Who is the Minister responding to Question No 17?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Allow me to, first, emphasise that every suicide, whether amongst youths, the middle-aged or the elderly, is one too many.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very sad, and we should endeavour to prevent them when we can.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A number of local studies have been done on suicide in the young.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These include efforts from agencies such as the Ministry of Health (MOH), the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), the Health Promotion Board (HPB), the Ministry of Education (MOE), and my Ministry.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Psychological resilience is crucial when youths face circumstances that overwhelm them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Within the school environment, HPB runs a series of psycho-emotional programmes to equip students with skills to manage stress and emotions, build positive and supportive relationships with peers, and recognise when and where to seek help.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Students may also be referred to school counsellors, community agencies and mental health professionals such as the Child Guidance Clinic in the IMH, where necessary.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MOE will further elaborate on its strategy to care for the socio-emotional well-being of students.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Outside of the schools, there is a strong network of community partners that have important roles in preventing teen suicide.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Healthcare and social service professionals are trained to identify and intervene appropriately when they come into contact with higher-risk individuals, such as those with a history of suicidal and self-harming behaviours.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) conducts programmes to teach teenagers how to identify suicide warning signs and where to seek help.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: SOS also runs a 24-hour crisis hotline, manned by trained adult volunteers, to counsel persons in distress.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Teenagers can play a role, certainly as friends, as fellow students, to look out for tell-tale signs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Or if we are concerned about the well-being of our friends, do let our teachers know or let the family know.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Several agencies such as MOH, IMH, MOE and my Ministry, have come together to further understand the triggers for suicide in the young and to devise effective strategies, including public education on prevention, towards building better mental resilience among our youths.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I think this will better inform inter-agency efforts to address the stressors and influences that drive young persons towards self-harm.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I would end by saying that all of us have a part to play; parents and family members to provide a supportive environment at home.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: All of us, as relatives, as friends, if we do pick up indicators that give us concern, do flag it up to the relevant authorities so that we can follow up.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is better to be Page: 30 safe than sorry.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Minister mentioned the strategies that have been taken holistically by cross-agencies to address teen suicide across the country.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I was wondering how far away Singapore is compared to international best practices in terms of handling of teen suicide.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Britain, for example, they have a teen suicide prevention strategy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are we moving towards that sort of strategy or campaign to address the teen suicide problem?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Our numbers, admittedly, while they are low, like I said, every suicide case is one too many.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have been tracking the numbers over the years.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They have been relatively stable, fluctuating in the last 10 years.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, in 2015, the numbers were a bit higher but no discernible patterns as of now.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are coming together to undertake a deeper study to understand whether there are new developments.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are surveying the various practices around the world to see what else we could put in place.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In a recent report from the Association of Women for Action and Research, secondary school students with depression reported being unable to access a trained counsellor at school because the teachers did not want her, who is a girl, to see a male counsellor, and faced uninformed and unhelpful remarks from teachers about her conditions, such as the teachers saying that she did not want to recover because she was smiling.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As teachers are always viewed as authority figures over these vulnerable young people, what sort of formal training do they have to ensure an informed and sensitive understanding of depression, other mental health difficulties and counselling?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They will be following up with a response subsequently but I would say that it would not be fair to highlight one specific example to reflect how our teachers approach these issues generally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I think teachers are trained, as far as possible, to pick up some of these concerns.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When these are flagged out in students, the teachers generally would refer them to the counsellors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There is a system in place in MOE.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is important for us to look at the entire system.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: From time to time, we would want to see how best to improve it and that is something we continue to want to do.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I can come back to the Member on that.
